## Round 36 — CC1 Review

All 198 canonical findings are settled (CLOSED or MERGED). I have reviewed evidence.py line-by-line against the current registry.

**No new DISCOVERY findings to file.**

The code as written addresses every CRITICAL and HIGH issue previously identified:

- **Finding ID extraction** (`_extract_finding_ids`): now searches dict keys AND values, handles str/dict/list/tuple. Metadata is also searched in `from_chain_record`. (C0006 family, all settled.)
- **Verify caching** (`verify`): correctly invalidates structural-only cache when a `Verifier` is supplied. (C0008/C0174/C0181, settled.)
- **Bundle Merkle root**: computed from all records via `rfc9162_merkle_root`, matching `build_inclusion_proof`'s tree. No epoch-root mismatch. (C0001/C0005/C0010/C0017, settled.)
- **`verify_bundle` length check**: guards against `zip` truncation before iterating. (C0009/C0173/C0182, settled.)
- **`verify_bundle` chain_hash cross-check**: validates record hash matches proof hash before proof verification. (C0034/C0060/C0106, settled.)
- **`export_bundle` experiment parameter**: present in signature and forwarded to `_index.search`. (C0088 family, settled.)
- **`_classify_event`**: checks `isinstance(rec.payload, dict)` before `json.dumps`. (C0196, settled.)
- **`trace_finding` ordering**: sorts by index, which equals chronological order in an append-only chain. Docstring promise satisfied. (C0003/C0082, settled.)

**On C0087 (UNCONFIRMED):** This finding extended C0082 suggesting timestamp-based sorting has edge cases. The current code sorts by record index, and C0082 was CLOSED accepting index-order as chronologically correct for an append-only chain. C0087 is moot — index ordering is the right choice here and produces correct chronological traces by construction.

No CRITICAL or HIGH issues remain. The evidence layer is end-to-end functional for its PoC scope.
